note: Datum's own state, as facts in Datum. Written because answering 'what is left, and what must the operator decide' required a forensic sweep of git, Fly's control plane, six reports and a todo list that had been overwritten - which is precisely the failure this store exists to abolish. Every open item is a mission with a machine-checkable gate. Every gate that only a human can close reads NO-EVIDENCE(confirmed-by-human), so 'what choices do I have to make' is one query and not an investigation.

assertions.subject: m2_store_only
assertions.claim: On the M2 re-run, Datum reading only the store scored 6.1 points over the better of the two baselines. The gate wanted 10.

evidence.method: 33 questions x 3 repeats x 4 arms, mechanical grader validated 26/26 on adversarial cases

assertions.why: The store-only arm is the architecture's own number. It fails the gate.

assertions.subject: m2_with_prose
assertions.claim: With the prose fallback wired into the read path, Datum scored 12.1 points over the better baseline, clearing the 10-point gate.

evidence.method: same 33 questions, same grading, prose fallback answered the three questions the store abstained on

assertions.why: The gate passes, but on an arm that reads material nobody asserted. Whether that counts is a decision, not a measurement.

assertions.subject: derived_edges
assertions.claim: 28% of derived code-graph edges resolve by a suffix index that cannot be reproduced from the artifact, so 72% are externally checkable.

evidence.method: limit test A over 19,495 symbols; no edge in the index is `measured` because tree-sitter is not a compiler

assertions.why: A label nobody outside Datum can check is a claim, not a derivation.

assertions.subject: symbol_identity
assertions.claim: Symbol keys embed the starting line, so inserting one line changes the identity of every symbol below it - inflating the measured change per commit 37x on edges.

evidence.method: 32 commits parsed at c^ and c under both identity rules: 887 edges vs 24

assertions.why: Incremental indexing has to answer 'is this the same symbol as last commit'. Today it cannot.

assertions.subject: full_reindex

object.detail: 3.7s parse + 2.1s load, for a commit that changed 2 of 965 files

assertions.claim: A two-file commit costs a full 5.8 second re-index of 966 files, repeating 99.6% of the work.

evidence.method: measured on real Arc at origin/master, 966 files, 19,177 symbols

assertions.subject: content_addressing

object.detail: 57,623 commit-file pairs vs 1,077 distinct blobs over 60 commits

assertions.claim: Storing the graph per file-version rather than per commit is 53.5x smaller on the real repository, and improves with history.

evidence.method: git ls-tree over the last 60 commits of origin/master, counting distinct blob shas

assertions.subject: stale_answer

object.detail: median change is 7 symbols and 24 edges of 102,450

assertions.claim: 88% of commits change the call graph, so an answer from the last indexed commit is right about the repository and wrong about the code being edited.

evidence.method: 32 commits, changed files parsed at c^ and at c, symbol and edge sets diffed under line-independent identity

assertions.why: This is the size of the gap a working-tree channel would close.

assertions.subject: overlay_payload

object.detail: 5.4 KB at p90, 24.3 KB at the worst of 60 commits

assertions.claim: Shipping parsed structure for the dirty files weighs 1.3 KB gzipped at the median, and Fly bills egress not ingress, so the remote-versus-local decision costs nothing either way.

evidence.method: indexer run over 2/4/8/26 real files, JSON serialised and gzipped

assertions.why: It removes cost from the argument. What is left is trust.

assertions.subject: monthly_cost
assertions.claim: The deployment costs $12.10/month against Fly Managed Postgres' $38 floor. An earlier table understated it by crediting the volume with a free allowance that belongs to snapshots.

evidence.method: rates read off Fly's pricing page for the sjc region on the day of the commit

missions.statement: Backups run in production, to a bucket outside the Fly organisation.

gates.subject: backup_bucket
gates.note: Which vendor and which account. Tigris, B2, R2 or S3. Nobody but the operator can decide it, and a backup inside the blast radius is not a backup.

gates.subject: backups
gates.note: The scripts are proven end to end against a real S3 API with real age encryption, 43 checks and 0 failures. Nothing is scheduled in production: one Machine, no cron, no bucket.

missions.statement: The admin password is not the one that was shared over chat.

gates.subject: admin_password
gates.note: It arrived in a chat transcript, so treat it as public. `npx @aeonmind/datum hash-password` then `fly secrets set`. The first API key was already revoked.

missions.statement: Symbol identity survives line drift, so a whitespace edit does not rename every symbol below it.

gates.subject: symbol_identity
gates.note: Prerequisite for incremental indexing, not a follow-up. No decision needed: this one is unambiguously a defect.

missions.statement: A commit is indexed without re-parsing the whole repository.

gates.subject: incremental_index
gates.note: Content-addressed blobs, a per-commit manifest, and an incremental resolver that can DEMOTE a derived edge to unverified when a new file makes its name ambiguous. Adding without demoting keeps serving a confident answer that is no longer justified.

gates.subject: incremental_index
gates.note: Today a two-file commit costs 5.8 seconds and 46 MB. Naive per-commit storage fills the 10 GB volume in 11 days.

missions.statement: An answer names which of its own files are dirty on the caller's disk.

gates.subject: staleness_channel
gates.note: Three options. Send nothing: MCP answers stay stale on 88% of edits. Send parsed structure: accurate mid-edit, but the server starts taking a client's word about its own disk. Send the dirty filenames only: ~100 bytes, exact staleness, and nothing unverified enters the graph. Recommended: filenames only.

gates.subject: staleness_channel
gates.note: A caveat that does not travel with the answer does not exist.

missions.statement: M2 passes on the store alone, without the prose fallback.

gates.subject: m2_store_only
gates.note: The gate already passes at +12.1 with prose. Store-only is +6.1. Whether the store alone must clear it is a decision about what the product claims, and §16 warns against rewriting the test after seeing the score.

gates.subject: m2_store_only
gates.note: It failed on coverage, never on correctness: zero wrong answers in 66 question-instances. Three of four misses were facts nobody had asserted.

missions.statement: A derived code edge can be checked by something other than Datum.

gates.subject: derived_edges
gates.note: tree-sitter is a parser, not a compiler, so no edge in the graph is `measured` and 28% of derived edges resolve by a suffix index an outsider cannot replicate. A compiler or LSP would produce the first genuinely measured edges. It is a real cost and a real dependency.

missions.statement: Indexing happens on push, without a human running a command.

gates.subject: indexing
gates.note: Today it is `datum index` then `datum ingest-graph`, by hand, which means the graph is stale the moment anyone commits and nothing says so.

meta.note: The only party who can close a confirmed-by-human gate on this project. Every mission blocked on a decision is blocked on this node.
